content: 1. Mifepristone reduces the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exercise caution and monitor. Use a backup contraceptive method. 2. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Exercise caution and monitor. 3. Nizatidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Exercise caution and monitor. 4. Mitotane reduces the levels of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4. Monitor when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates for potential dosage adjustments. 5. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol due to plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dose adjustment of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. 6. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Exercise caution and monitor. 7. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism
